newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis bids ease as board rises.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis bids ease as board rises.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat eased as KCBT wheat futures climbed up their 25-cent per bushel limit, grain merchandisers in the U.S. High Plains said Tuesday.
Dealers said movement had been slow Monday as growers held out for further price gains.
"Everybody's bulled up so nobody wanted to sell any wheat But since we're not being called limit-up today, I'd guess we're going to buy a whole lot more," a Kansas dealer said.
Dealers said they were still uncertain how much wheat was damaged as a result of the weekend freeze.

"We did have a couple of agronomists in south-central Kansas saying that if conditions were favorable from here on out, we could raise a normal crop," another Kansas dealer said. "But everybody thinks it's going to be another week until we know exactly how much was damaged."

The weekly Kansas crop weather report, released Monday, said the extent of damage is currently unknown. But if damage were to have taken place, most of it would have occurred in southern areas of the state where more wheat had jointed and snow was lacking.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
